channel.title: MINI recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: BMW, Mini Integrated Brake System May Malfunction
item.description: The integrated brake system in these vehicles may malfunction. This can cause a loss of power brake assist, which affects how the brakes work. It can also cause the Antilock Brake System and the Dynamic Stability Control system to stop functioning properly. To fix this, the integrated brake system will be inspected and, if necessary, replaced, free of charge for owners.

item.title: BMW X1, X2, Mini Countryman Seat Belt Retractor Damage
item.description: In certain BMW X1, X2, and Mini Countryman S ALL4 vehicles, the torsion bar inside both front seat belt retractors may have been damaged during manufacturing.

item.title: Mini Countryman Front Structure Bolts Loose
item.description: BMW is recalling certain 228i, 228i xDrive, and MINI Countryman S ALL4 vehicles because the bolts that connect the front body structure to the vehicle's chassis may not have been tightened properly. If these bolts are not tight enough, the connection between the front body structure and the chassis may be looser than it is supposed to be, rather than fully secure as intended for these vehicles' front structure.

item.title: BMW and MINI Brake System Weld May Fail
item.description: The welds inside the servomotor of the integrated brake control module may break. If this happens, the vehicle can lose power assist for the brakes and lose function in the rear brakes. The antilock brake system and the dynamic stability control system may also stop working properly. To fix the problem, BMW dealers will replace the entire integrated brake system with a new one.

item.title: MINI Cooper SE High Voltage Battery Fire Risk
item.description: On some MINI Hardtop 2 Door (Cooper SE) vehicles, a fault can occur in the high voltage battery or the high voltage electrical system, which can lead to a short circuit. A short circuit like this raises the risk of a fire.

item.title: MINI Countryman Armrest May Detach in Crash
item.description: Some MINI Countryman S ALL4 and JCW Countryman ALL4 vehicles have a rear side door armrest support bracket that may not be properly secured. Because of this, the armrest could come loose and detach from the door panel if the side air bag deploys during a crash. A detached armrest could then strike a rear seat passenger, or it could get in the way of the air bag deploying the way it is supposed to.

item.title: MINI Cooper SE Battery Water Leak Fire Risk
item.description: The seal on the high-voltage battery housing may not have been done properly, which can let water get into the battery. Water damage to the battery can cause a fire or make the vehicle stall. Dealers will inspect and leak-test the battery, and repair it as needed, free of charge.

item.title: BMW, Mini Brake System May Lose Power Assist
item.description: The integrated brake system in these vehicles may malfunction. This can cause a loss of power brake assist, which affects how the brakes work. It can also cause the Antilock Brake System and the Dynamic Stability Control system to stop functioning properly. To fix this, dealers will replace the integrated brake system, and this repair is free of charge for owners.

item.title: BMW, MINI and Toyota Supra passenger seat belt retractor fault
item.description: BMW is recalling certain BMW, MINI, Rolls Royce and Toyota Supra vehicles. The passenger seat belt has a locking feature that can switch off too early, before the belt webbing has pulled all the way back in. Because of this, these seat belt assemblies do not meet the federal safety standard for occupant crash protection. Dealers will inspect the seat belt retractors and the seat belts themselves, and replace the retractors if that is needed.

item.title: BMW, MINI Hybrid Battery Debris Fire Risk
item.description: Certain plug-in hybrid BMW and MINI models, along with the BMW i8, may have debris that got into one or more cells of the high-voltage hybrid battery during manufacturing. This debris can cause a short-circuit inside the battery. A short-circuit like this raises the chance of a fire starting in the vehicle, or of someone being injured.

item.title: BMW and Mini Plug-In Hybrid Battery Fire Risk
item.description: In certain plug-in hybrid BMW and MINI models, loose metal welding beads inside the hybrid battery could form a conductive path between battery cells that are not supposed to be connected to each other. This stray connection could cause the battery to short-circuit. Dealers will inspect the battery modules and replace them if necessary, and the repair is free of charge for the owner.

item.title: BMW X1/X2 and MINI airbags may fail in rollover
item.description: BMW is recalling certain X1, X2, and MINI models because of a problem with the sensor that detects a rollover, located inside the airbag control unit. If the vehicle is in a rollover crash, this problem could mean the head airbags, seat belt pretensioners, and other safety systems don't activate the way they're supposed to.

item.title: MINI Cooper Rear Trim Missing Crash Pad
item.description: MINI is recalling certain Cooper, Cooper S, and JCW hardtop 2-door vehicles because the rear side trim panels may have been installed without a crash pad. Without this pad, rear seat passengers have an increased risk of injury if the vehicle is in a side-impact crash. Because of this missing part, these vehicles do not meet a federal safety standard for side impact protection.

item.title: BMW X1, X2, MINI Cooper Steering Tie Rod May Break
item.description: Some BMW X1, X2, and MINI Cooper vehicles may have a steering tie rod that wasn't assembled correctly. Over time, this can cause the tie rod end to wear down more than it should, and it could eventually break.

item.title: Mini Countryman Missing Fuel Pump Crash Plate
item.description: On some Countryman vehicles, a metal plate meant to protect the high-pressure fuel pump from crash damage may be missing. Without this crash protection plate in place, the fuel pump could become damaged if the vehicle is in a crash, which could then cause fuel to leak from the vehicle.

item.title: BMW, MINI: Crankshaft Sensor May Cause Stalling
item.description: On certain BMW and MINI vehicles, the crankshaft sensor may be installed with incorrect firmware. This incorrect firmware can prevent the sensor from properly reading signals from the crankshaft reluctor ring. As a result, the vehicle may stall while it is being driven. BMW will notify owners, and dealers will replace the crankshaft sensor, free of charge, to correct the problem.

item.title: Mini Clubman and Countryman Trailer Hitch May Separate
item.description: Some trailer hitches installed on Mini Clubman and Countryman vehicles may not have enough support where they attach to the vehicle. Under certain loads, the hitch can sag, and in some cases it could separate from the vehicle entirely.
